title: Griess Test Protocol
author: Tamiris Silva
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.96ph9dn

steps.title: Prepare Sodium Nitrite Standard Solution
steps.instruction: Prepare a 10mM (10,000µM) sodium nitrite solution for the standard curve.

substeps.instruction: Dissolve 0.06899g NaNO2 in 100 mL distilled water.
Store the solution in a dark flask at room temperature.

steps.title: Prepare Standard Curve Serial Dilutions
steps.instruction: Prepare a series of nitrite concentrations using 7 identified microtubes.

substeps.instruction: In the first microtube, add 8 µL of nitrite (10mM/10,000µM) and 492 µL PBS.
Transfer 250 µL from the initial tube to the second to last tube (which must contain 250 µL for serial dilution) to achieve a final volume of 250 µL.

steps.title: Set Up 96-Well Plate Assay
steps.instruction: Dispense samples and standards into a 96-well plate.

substeps.instruction: Add 50 µL of each standard concentration to quadruplicate wells.
Add 50 µL of serum sample to the designated wells.
Use the last well for a blank containing supplemented culture medium only.

steps.title: Develop Color Reaction
steps.instruction: Add Griess reagent to the plate to develop the assay.

substeps.instruction: Add 50 µL of Griess reagent to all wells containing samples and the standard curve.
